title: Close Recap: Nasdaq Rebounds 1.09% to 24,579; Dow Slips 237 Points; DraftKings Plunges on Forecast Cut
dek: The Nasdaq Composite closed up 1.09% at 24,579.42 and the S&P 500 rose 0.31% to 7,376.86. The Dow fell 237.33 points to 51,285.73. Chips led the bounce, while DraftKings shares were hit hard after cutting its profit outlook.
author: Meridian Newsroom

keyPoints: Nasdaq Composite closed up 1.09% at 24,579.42, and the S&P 500 rose 0.31% to 7,376.86 (CNBC live updates; Investrade's closing recap shows the S&P 500 up 0.32%).
The Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 237.33 points, or 0.46%, to settle at 51,285.73 (CNBC live updates; Investrade shows a 236.85-point drop).
The Russell 2000 gained 0.89% to 2,754 (Investrade closing recap).

DraftKings fell about 25.9% to $17.44 on the day after a Q3 miss and a cut to its 2026 profit outlook (GuruFocus). Intraday it traded as low as $16.55, down 29.6% from the $23.52 prior close (24/7 Wall St.).

Week-to-date, Investrade put the Dow down 0.94%, the S&P 500 down 2.68% and the Nasdaq down 3.37%. Those figures differ from other week totals in our midday coverage, which should be read with that in mind.
body:
## The close

U.S. stocks rebounded on Friday after Thursday's AI-led rout. The Nasdaq Composite closed up 1.09% at 24,579.42, according to CNBC's live coverage. The S&P 500 rose 0.31% to 7,376.86, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 237.33 points, or 0.46%, to 51,285.73. Investrade's closing table gives slightly different percentage moves for the S&P 500 (+0.32%) and the Dow (-0.46%), with a 236.85-point Dow loss; the levels agree.

The Russell 2000 gained 0.89% to 2,754, Investrade reported.

## Thursday's damage, and the week

Thursday's session was the reference point for Friday's rebound. Zacks reported that the Nasdaq Composite fell 5.5% to 24,315.00 and the S&P 500 fell 4.4% to 7,353.73 on Thursday, while the Dow fell 3.4% to 51,523.06. The Philadelphia semiconductor index fell more than 12%, according to the same report.

For the week, Investrade put the Dow down 0.94%, the S&P 500 down 2.68% and the Nasdaq down 3.37%. Trading Economics figures quoted in our midday rebound story put the week's losses larger (Nasdaq about 4.4%, S&P 500 nearly 3%, Dow about 0.5%). We have not been able to reconcile those two sets of weekly figures, so we present Investrade's numbers as the close-week summary and flag the gap here.

Investrade also said XLK fell about 8% on the week and XLE about 12%. The Nasdaq 100 closed down 6.4% on Thursday, its worst day since March 2020, and remained in a correction from its Oct. 6 record.

## Volatility

The VIX jumped 69.7% on Thursday to about 28.18, its biggest one-day percentage gain since December 2024, according to TheStreet and Zacks. On Friday it fell 15.73%, Yahoo Finance's quote page showed. Applying that decline to Thursday's close implies a level near 23.7, but that level is derived and was not printed in the sources we fetched.

## Movers: DraftKings

DraftKings was the day's biggest single-stock casualty. Bloomberg reported shares fell as much as 29% after the company cut its profit forecast on continued spending on its prediction-market product. GuruFocus reported a close near $17.44, down 25.85%. The roughly 21% figure in the assignment brief did not match the sources we checked, which put the close nearer 26%. Benzinga reported an adjusted loss of 53 cents a share in the third quarter, wider than the 39-cent loss expected.

## Why it matters

The rebound came on chips, which carry the most direct exposure to the AI-spending worry, but the week still closed with heavy losses in technology and energy. Investors now look to next week's CPI print and a slate of tech earnings, including Applied Materials, Nebius, CoreWeave and Cisco, as the next tests for the AI trade.

marketImpact.summary: The close shows a partial repair after the worst Nasdaq session in months, but the week's losses in technology and energy are still large. DraftKings' collapse shows how sharply the market is punishing spending that cuts near-term profit.
marketImpact.timeframe: Friday, Nov. 6 close, and the coming week's inflation and tech earnings
